blocks.h2: When Gas Piping Needs a Plumber

bodies: We find gas leaks with electronic detectors and fitting-by-fitting tests, then pressure-test the system to confirm it's tight.
In older Evanston homes, leaks often show up at old unions and valves, on branches left from removed appliances and at fittings near the meter. After the repair, Nicor Gas can restore service.

blocks.intro: Gas piping in older homes has often been changed many times.

items.body: More joints, more chances to leak.
Old lines to removed appliances need to be capped properly.

blocks.h2: Gas Piping in Older Evanston Homes
blocks.body: In a house that's been updated several times, the gas piping tells the story. You'll often find a branch to a long-gone stove, a line that once fed a gas light or a dryer connection in the wrong room. Each one is a set of fittings that can loosen over time. When we repair a leak, we also look for these abandoned branches and cap them properly, so the system has fewer places to fail.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Questions From Evanston Homeowners

items.q: What should I do if I smell gas?
items.preview: Leave and call Nicor Gas or 911.
items.answer: Leave without touching switches. Call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside, then call us.

items.q: Who is responsible for gas piping?
items.preview: Nicor up to the meter. You after it.
items.answer: Nicor Gas handles everything up to and including the meter. Piping after the meter belongs to the homeowner.

items.q: Can you cap old gas lines?
items.answer: Yes, and we pressure-test the system after.

items.q: How long until service is restored?
items.answer: Once we repair and test the line, Nicor Gas can restore service.

items.q: Is a faint gas smell near the stove normal?
items.preview: A brief whiff when lighting can be. A steady smell isn't.
items.answer: A brief smell when a burner lights can happen. A steady smell is not normal. Leave and call Nicor Gas.

items.q: How much does gas line repair cost in Evanston?
items.preview: It depends on the leak. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the leak is and how much pipe needs work. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
